steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Economic growth is an increase in the value of goods and services produced in an economy over time, usually measured by GDP (Gross Domestic Product). | Key Fact: Real GDP adjusts for inflation (uses constant prices), giving a true picture of whether output actually increased. GDP per capita = GDP / population, indicating average living standards. | Key Fact: Causes of growth: increase in quantity/quality of factors of production, technological progress, increased investment, improved education and training, and population growth. | Key Fact: Benefits of growth: higher incomes, improved living standards, lower unemployment, increased tax revenue (for public services), and greater consumer choice.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the difference between GDP, real GDP, and GDP per capita. | Describe three benefits and two costs of economic growth. | Evaluate whether economic growth always improves living standards.
